Where do late orders spend more time?

On timeLate

Median hours share one zero-based scale. Stages have no comparable transit target in this dataset; distributions describe elapsed time, not responsibility. Grouping by the delivery outcome cannot establish a cause. Stage medians do not sum to the median total.

Earliest item deadline check

Order-level carrier handoff is compared with the earliest recorded item shipping deadline. Multi-item and multi-seller orders make this a proxy, not a seller compliance measure.

Seller-associated orders to inspect

Single-seller orders across the full window; lowest observed on-time rates first.

Showing the first 10 qualifying sellers. Rates reflect seller-associated orders, including customer locations and delivery estimates. 95% Wilson intervals show binomial sampling uncertainty only; clustering, route mix and censoring are not adjusted.

Evidence and definitions

The main KPI is on-time rate among delivered orders with valid dates: A/(A+L). U is unconfirmed, X is canceled or unavailable; neither enters that denominator. Coverage = (A+L)/(A+L+U). Estimated delivery dates are customer estimates.

The last cohorts may be right-censored. The 31-day default horizon admits 74 weeks; 45 and 60 days admit 72 and 70. These are different windows, not confidence intervals. Olist provides no carrier identifiers.

Calculation checks and source files

Calculations use one row per order and independent DuckDB queries from the raw files. Source hashes and the current mart fingerprint are in the lineage receipt.
